Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (the product formula (PF) and its extension to integrable and a.e.-Borel integrands), recast as an identity of measures; the extensions then follow by general measure theory (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff, MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff) and are carried out in the sibling children. In the parent, the lintegral hypothesis is part (b) of the sibling DAG node iwl_cr_hausdorff_product_formula.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k]; S := π⁻¹(A) = {y : π(y) ∈ A}; ν := Hᵐ⌞A; Φ′ : ℝ × ℝ^P → ℝ^{P+1}, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2); L¹ := volume on ℝ.

1. (ν is σ-finite.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so ν(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ A) = Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply). Thus ν is finite on compact sets; since ℝ^P = ⋃_n B̄(0, n) is σ-compact, ν is σ-finite (instance SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), in particular s-finite, so Measure.prod_apply applies to L¹ ⊗ ν.
2. (Φ′ is Borel.) EuclideanSpace.equiv and its inverse are continuous linear equivalences and p ↦ Fin.cons p.1 (equiv p.2) is continuous (Continuous.finCons, continuous_fst, continuous_snd). Hence Φ′ is continuous, so Borel measurable, and Φ′⁻¹(B) is Borel for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^{P+1}.
3. (Left side.) Let B ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} be Borel. Then (H^{m+1}⌞S)(B) = ∫⁻ 1_B d(H^{m+1}⌞S) = ∫⁻_S 1_B dH^{m+1} (lintegral_indicator_one).
4. (Hypothesis.) 1_B is Borel and [0,∞]-valued, so by the hypothesis ∫⁻_S 1_B dH^{m+1} = ∫⁻_ℝ ∫⁻_A 1_B(Φ(s, x)) dHᵐ(x) ds.
5. (Sections.) Fix s ∈ ℝ and let C_s := (Prod.mk s)⁻¹(Φ′⁻¹(B)) = {x : Φ(s, x) ∈ B}, a Borel set (measurable_prodMk_left). Then 1_B(Φ(s, x)) = 1_{C_s}(x) for every x, so ∫⁻_A 1_B(Φ(s, x)) dHᵐ(x) = ∫⁻ 1_{C_s} dν = ν(C_s) (lintegral_indicator_one).
6. (Product measure.) By Measure.prod_apply (Φ′⁻¹(B) is Borel, ν is s-finite), ∫⁻_ℝ ν(C_s) ds = (L¹ ⊗ ν)(Φ′⁻¹(B)), and by Measure.map_apply (Φ′ measurable, B Borel) this equals (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν))(B).
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–6 give (H^{m+1}⌞S)(B) = (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν))(B) for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^{P+1}. Two measures on ℝ^{P+1} that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext). Hence H^{m+1}⌞π⁻¹(A) = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A). ∎

Source: Step 3 of the parent proof (“blow-ups of the product are products of blow-ups”; dominated convergence in the interval variable), with the product formula of Step 1 in the measure form (MP). Instead of applying (PF) to the blow-ups M_r, the blow-ups are undone by the blow-up change of variables (sibling blowup_cov = the accepted declaration fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral), so (MP) is only applied to A = M and to the plane A = T.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))); π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))); y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0; Φ′ : ℝ × E → E′, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = Φ(1, 0); ι(v) := Φ(0, v); M̃ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)}; θ̃ := θ ∘ π (Lean: fun y => θ (π y)); O := {y ∈ E′ : y₀ ∈ (0,1)} (open), so M̃ = O ∩ {π ∈ M}. (MP) denotes the hypothesis: for every A ⊆ E that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A).
Coordinate facts (all by Fin.cons/Fin.tail computations, ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_self_tail): (F1) π(Φ(s,u)) = u, (Φ(s,u))₀ = s and Φ(y₀, π(y)) = y; (F2) Φ is linear: Φ(s,u) − Φ(s′,u′) = Φ(s − s′, u − u′), Φ(s,u) + Φ(s′,u′) = Φ(s + s′, u + u′), c·Φ(s,u) = Φ(cs, cu); in particular ι is linear and π is linear; (F3) ⟨Φ(a,u), Φ(b,w)⟩ = ab + ⟨u,w⟩ (sum over Fin (P+1) split by Fin.sum_univ_succ), hence ‖Φ(s,u)‖² = s² + ‖u‖², |s| ≤ ‖Φ(s,u)‖ and ‖u‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s,u)‖; (F4) Φ′ is a homeomorphism ℝ × E → E′ with continuous inverse y ↦ (y₀, π(y)) (Continuous.finCons, continuous_pi), hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding); in particular Φ′ and π are Borel measurable.
Further notation. y* := Φ(s₀, x); T := span τ; τ̃ := (e₀, ιτ_1, …, ιτ_m); Q := span τ̃; ν := Hᵐ⌞M; ρ := (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν. For r > 0, η_r := blowUpMap y* r (η_r(z) = r⁻¹(z − y*)) on E′ and η′_r := blowUpMap x r on E. The sibling blowup_cov states: for every n, every centre c, every r > 0, every set S and every function g, ∫_{blowUpMap c r '' S} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(blowUpMap c r z) dHⁿ(z) (no measurability or integrability assumption).

1. (τ̃ is orthonormal; dim Q = m + 1; dim T = m.) By (F3): ‖e₀‖² = 1 + ‖0‖² = 1; ‖ιτ_i‖ = ‖τ_i‖ = 1; ⟨e₀, ιτ_i⟩ = 1·0 + ⟨0, τ_i⟩ = 0; ⟨ιτ_i, ιτ_j⟩ = 0·0 + ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = 0 for i ≠ j. Hence τ̃ is orthonormal, so linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), and finrank Q = card (Fin (m+1)) = m + 1 (finrank_span_eq_card). Likewise finrank T = m.
2. (Q = {z : π(z) ∈ T} as sets.) π is linear, so Z := {z : π(z) ∈ T} is a linear subspace (the comap of T). It contains e₀ (π(e₀) = 0 ∈ T) and every ιτ_i (π(ιτ_i) = τ_i ∈ T), so Q ⊆ Z (Submodule.span_le). Conversely, if π(z) ∈ T, write π(z) = Σ_i c_i τ_i (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); by (F1), (F2), z = Φ(z₀, π(z)) = z₀·e₀ + Σ_i c_i·ιτ_i ∈ Q.
3. (Measure identities.) (a) M satisfies the hypotheses of (MP) (null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable, Hᵐ(M ∩ K) < ∞), and ν is σ-finite: it is finite on compacts (ν(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ M) < ∞ for compact, hence Borel, K; Measure.restrict_apply), so SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts applies. O is open, hence Borel, Φ′⁻¹(O) = (0,1) × E by (F1), and M̃ = O ∩ {π ∈ M}. Hence H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = (H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ M})⌞O (Measure.restrict_restrict) = (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν))⌞O (MP) = Φ′_*((L¹ ⊗ ν)⌞((0,1) × E)) (Measure.restrict_map, Φ′ measurable) = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν) = Φ′_*ρ (Measure.prod_restrict, Measure.restrict_univ). (b) The plane T satisfies the hypotheses of (MP): T is closed (finite-dimensional subspace, Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence Borel and null-measurable; T is the range of Λ : Eucl m → E, Λ(u) := Σ_i u_i τ_i (u_i the coordinates of u), which is a linear isometry because τ is orthonormal (‖Λu‖² = Σ_i u_i² = ‖u‖²), so LipschitzWith 1 Λ and T is countably m-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_range; range Λ = span τ by Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); and since finrank T = m, Hᵐ⌞T is a regular, in particular finite-on-compacts, measure (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule; alternatively Hᵐ⌞T = Λ_*(Hᵐ on Eucl m) = Λ_*(volume) by Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, and Λ⁻¹(K) is compact), so Hᵐ(T ∩ K) = (Hᵐ⌞T)(K) < ∞ for compact K. Therefore H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ T} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T), and Hᵐ⌞T is σ-finite.
4. (Measurability of θ.) For each n ∈ ℕ, θ is Hᵐ-integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable, on M ∩ B̄(0, n); since M = ⋃_n (M ∩ B̄(0, n)), θ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Consequently (s, u) ↦ θ(u) is a.e. strongly measurable for ρ (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd), and products of θ with continuous functions are a.e. strongly measurable for ν and ρ. Also, ν-a.e. u lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀, M null-measurable), so θ(u) ≥ 0 for ν-a.e. u.
5. (Fix f.) Let f ∈ C_c(E′). Choose R ≥ 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄(0, R) and C_f ≥ 0 with |f(z)| ≤ C_f for all z (continuous with compact support). By (F3): (*) if f(Φ(σ, w)) ≠ 0 then |σ| ≤ R and ‖w‖ ≤ R.
6. (Notation.) For σ ∈ ℝ let f_σ(w) := f(Φ(σ, w)); f_σ is continuous and by (*) its support lies in B̄(0, R), so f_σ ∈ C_c(E). For r > 0 put A(r) := ∫_{η_r(M̃)} f(z) θ̃(y* + r z) dH^{m+1}(z) (the integral in Simon 1.7 for (M̃, θ̃) at y*) and a_r(σ) := ∫_{η′_r(M)} f_σ(w) θ(x + r w) dHᵐ(w) (the integral in Simon 1.7 for (M, θ) at x with test function f_σ).
7. (Undoing the blow-ups.) Let r > 0. blowup_cov in E′ with n = m + 1, c = y*, S = M̃ and g(z) = f(z)θ̃(y* + r z), together with y* + r·r⁻¹(w − y*) = w, gives A(r) = (r^{m+1})⁻¹ ∫_{M̃} f(η_r(w)) θ(π(w)) dH^{m+1}(w). blowup_cov in E with n = m, c = x, S = M and g(w) = f_σ(w)θ(x + r w), together with x + r·η′_r(u) = u, gives a_r(σ) = (r^m)⁻¹ h_r(σ), where h_r(σ) := ∫_M f(Φ(σ, η′_r(u))) θ(u) dHᵐ(u).
8. (Blow-ups of products are products of blow-ups.) By (F2), η_r(Φ(s, u)) = r⁻¹(Φ(s, u) − Φ(s₀, x)) = Φ(r⁻¹(s − s₀), η′_r(u)).
9. (Fubini.) Let G_r(s, u) := f(Φ(r⁻¹(s − s₀), η′_r(u))) θ(u). By Step 3(a), MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (F4) (valid for every integrand), Step 8 and (F1): ∫_{M̃} f(η_r(w)) θ(π(w)) dH^{m+1}(w) = ∫ G_r dρ. G_r is ρ-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable (Step 4); by (*), G_r(s, u) ≠ 0 forces ‖η′_r(u)‖ ≤ R, i.e. u ∈ B̄(x, rR), so |G_r(s, u)| ≤ C_f |θ(u)| 1_{B̄(x, rR)}(u); and (s, u) ↦ |θ(u)| 1_{B̄(x, rR)}(u) is ρ-integrable because θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄(x, rR) (compact) and L¹⌞(0,1) is finite (Integrable.comp_snd). By Fubini (integral_prod), ∫ G_r dρ = ∫_{(0,1)} H_r(s) ds with H_r(s) := ∫_M G_r(s, u) dHᵐ(u).
10. (Change of variables in the interval variable.) ∫_{(0,1)} H_r(s) ds = ∫_0^1 H_r(s) ds (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le gives the integral over (0,1], and integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo since {1} is L¹-null). Put a_r := −s₀/r and b_r := (1 − s₀)/r, so a_r < 0 < b_r, r·a_r + s₀ = 0 and r·b_r + s₀ = 1. intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_add (c = r ≠ 0, d = s₀) gives ∫_{a_r}^{b_r} H_r(rσ + s₀) dσ = r⁻¹ ∫_0^1 H_r(s) ds. Since r⁻¹((rσ + s₀) − s₀) = σ, H_r(rσ + s₀) = h_r(σ) = r^m a_r(σ) (Step 7). Combining Steps 7, 9 and 10: A(r) = (r^{m+1})⁻¹ · r · r^m ∫_{a_r}^{b_r} a_r(σ) dσ = ∫_ℝ 1_{(a_r, b_r]}(σ) a_r(σ) dσ for every r > 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, integral_indicator).
11. (Pointwise limit.) Fix σ ∈ ℝ. The tangent hypothesis for (M, θ) at x, applied to f_σ ∈ C_c(E), gives a_r(σ) → θ(x) ∫_T f_σ dHᵐ as r → 0⁺. Since 0 < s₀ < 1, a_r → −∞ and b_r → +∞ as r → 0⁺, so σ ∈ (a_r, b_r] for all sufficiently small r > 0. Hence 1_{(a_r, b_r]}(σ) a_r(σ) → θ(x) ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w) as r → 0⁺, for every σ.
12. (Uniform domination.) Let g₀(w) := max(0, min(1, R + 1 − ‖w‖)). Then g₀ ∈ C_c(E), 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ 1, g₀ = 1 on B̄(0, R) and g₀ = 0 off B̄(0, R + 1). Put b(r) := ∫_{η′_r(M)} g₀(w) θ(x + r w) dHᵐ(w); by blowup_cov as in Step 7, b(r) = (r^m)⁻¹ ∫_M g₀(η′_r(u)) θ(u) dHᵐ(u). The tangent hypothesis applied to g₀ gives b(r) → θ(x) ∫_T g₀ dHᵐ as r → 0⁺, so there is r₀ > 0 with b(r) ≤ B₀ := θ(x) ∫_T g₀ dHᵐ + 1 for 0 < r < r₀. For ν-a.e. u (namely u ∈ M) and every σ, |f(Φ(σ, η′_r(u))) θ(u)| ≤ C_f g₀(η′_r(u)) θ(u): θ(u) ≥ 0, and if f(Φ(σ, η′_r(u))) ≠ 0 then ‖η′_r(u)‖ ≤ R by (*), so g₀(η′_r(u)) = 1. The function u ↦ C_f g₀(η′_r(u)) θ(u) is ν-integrable (a.e. strongly measurable, bounded by C_f |θ(u)| 1_{B̄(x, r(R+1))}(u)). Hence |h_r(σ)| ≤ C_f ∫_M g₀(η′_r(u)) θ(u) dHᵐ(u) (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le), i.e. |a_r(σ)| ≤ C_f b(r) ≤ K₀ := C_f B₀ for all σ and all 0 < r < r₀. Moreover, if |σ| > R then f(Φ(σ, ·)) ≡ 0 by (*), so a_r(σ) = 0. Therefore |1_{(a_r, b_r]}(σ) a_r(σ)| ≤ K₀ 1_{[−R, R]}(σ) for every σ and every 0 < r < r₀, and K₀ 1_{[−R, R]} is L¹-integrable.
13. (Measurability in σ.) For r > 0, σ ↦ h_r(σ) is continuous (continuous_of_dominated): for each σ, u ↦ f(Φ(σ, η′_r(u))) θ(u) is a.e. strongly measurable for ν; it is bounded by C_f |θ(u)| 1_{B̄(x, rR)}(u), a ν-integrable function independent of σ (by (*)); and σ ↦ f(Φ(σ, η′_r(u))) θ(u) is continuous for every u. Hence σ ↦ 1_{(a_r, b_r]}(σ) a_r(σ) = 1_{(a_r, b_r]}(σ) (r^m)⁻¹ h_r(σ) is a.e. strongly measurable.
14. (Dominated convergence.) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 is countably generated. By Steps 10–13 and tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence, A(r) → ∫_ℝ θ(x) ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w) dσ = θ(x) ∫_ℝ ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w) dσ as r → 0⁺ (integral_mul_left; the identity of Step 10 holds for all r > 0, i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, so Tendsto.congr' applies).
15. (Identification of the limit.) By Step 3(b) and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, ∫_{π⁻¹(T)} f dH^{m+1} = ∫ f∘Φ′ d(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T). The function f∘Φ′ is continuous, and by (*) it is bounded by C_f 1_{[−R, R]}(σ) 1_{B̄(0, R)}(w), which is L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T-integrable because Hᵐ(T ∩ B̄(0, R)) < ∞ (Step 3(b); Integrable.mul_prod). By Fubini (integral_prod), ∫ f∘Φ′ d(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T) = ∫_ℝ ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w) dσ. By Step 2, (Q : Set E′) = π⁻¹(T). Hence the limit in Step 14 equals θ(x) ∫_Q f dH^{m+1} = θ̃(y*) ∫_Q f dH^{m+1}, since θ̃(y*) = θ(π(Φ(s₀, x))) = θ(x) by (F1).
16. (Conclusion.) finrank Q = m + 1 (Step 1), and for every f ∈ C_c(E′), ∫_{blowUpMap y* r '' M̃} f(z) θ̃(y* + r·z) dH^{m+1}(z) → θ̃(y*) ∫_Q f dH^{m+1} as r → 0⁺ (Steps 5–15). This is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m+1) M̃ θ̃ (Φ s₀ x) Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ̃ = (e₀, ιτ) is orthonormal, so finrank span τ̃ = m + 1, and span τ̃ = π⁻¹(span τ) as sets.
(MP) for M and the restriction to O give H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ Hᵐ⌞M); (MP) also applies to the plane T = span τ.
blowup_cov undoes both blow-ups: A(r) = (r^{m+1})⁻¹∫_{M̃} f(η_r w)θ(πw) and a_r(σ) = (r^m)⁻¹∫_M f(Φ(σ, η′_r u))θ(u).
η_r(Φ(s,u)) = Φ(r⁻¹(s − s₀), η′_r u); Fubini and the substitution s = s₀ + rσ give A(r) = ∫ 1_{(−s₀/r, (1−s₀)/r]}(σ) a_r(σ) dσ.
Pointwise a_r(σ) → θ(x)∫_T f(Φ(σ,·)) by the tangent hypothesis, and the indicator tends to 1 since 0 < s₀ < 1.
Domination |a_r(σ)| ≤ C_f b(r) ≤ K₀ for small r via a cut-off g₀ and the tangent hypothesis for g₀; a_r(σ) = 0 for |σ| > R; continuity in σ gives measurability.
Dominated convergence gives A(r) → θ(x)∫_ℝ∫_T f(Φ(σ,w)) = θ̃(Φ(s₀,x))∫_Q f by (MP) for T and Fubini.

subproblems.title: The product triple ((0,1) × M, θ∘π, e₀ ∧ ξ∘π) is a rectifiable triple
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k], with Φ, π, Φ′, y₀, e₀ = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 and ι(v) = Φ(0, v) as in the parent, and assume (MP): for every A ⊆ ℝ^P that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A). Let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple univ m M θ ξ in ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1, as in the frozen contract) with θ ≥ 1 on M. Then there is ξ′ : ℝ^{P+1} → Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) (NVector (Eucl (P+1)) (m+1)) such that IsRectifiableTriple univ (m+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ′ holds for M̃ := {y : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0, 1)} and θ̃ := θ ∘ π, and such that ξ′(Φ(s, x))(α) = ξ(x)(β) for all s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P, α ∈ Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) and β ∈ Λ^m(ℝ^P) with β(v) = α(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_m) for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m (i.e. ξ′ = e₀ ∧ ξ∘π, Simon 3.2(2)).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof (the product triple Π = τ((0,1) × M, θ∘π_2, e₀ ∧ ξ∘π_2), Simon 3.2(2)), with the product formula of Step 1 in the measure form (MP), and with the weighted tangent condition (parent Step 3) supplied by the sibling product_tangent (iwl_cr_ip_product_weighted_tangent).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))); π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))); y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0; Φ′ : ℝ × E → E′, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = Φ(1, 0); ι(v) := Φ(0, v); M̃ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)}; θ̃ := θ ∘ π (Lean: fun y => θ (π y)); O := {y ∈ E′ : y₀ ∈ (0,1)} (open), so M̃ = O ∩ {π ∈ M}. (MP) denotes the hypothesis: for every A ⊆ E that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A).
Coordinate facts (all by Fin.cons/Fin.tail computations, ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_self_tail): (F1) π(Φ(s,u)) = u, (Φ(s,u))₀ = s and Φ(y₀, π(y)) = y; (F2) Φ is linear: Φ(s,u) − Φ(s′,u′) = Φ(s − s′, u − u′), Φ(s,u) + Φ(s′,u′) = Φ(s + s′, u + u′), c·Φ(s,u) = Φ(cs, cu); in particular ι is linear and π is linear; (F3) ⟨Φ(a,u), Φ(b,w)⟩ = ab + ⟨u,w⟩ (sum over Fin (P+1) split by Fin.sum_univ_succ), hence ‖Φ(s,u)‖² = s² + ‖u‖², |s| ≤ ‖Φ(s,u)‖ and ‖u‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s,u)‖; (F4) Φ′ is a homeomorphism ℝ × E → E′ with continuous inverse y ↦ (y₀, π(y)) (Continuous.finCons, continuous_pi), hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding); in particular Φ′ and π are Borel measurable.
Derived facts from (MP) used below. (D1) (null sets) If N ⊆ E and Hᵐ(N) = 0 then H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0: N is Hᵐ-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.of_null), countably m-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero) and Hᵐ(N ∩ K) ≤ Hᵐ(N) = 0 < ∞, so by (MP) H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ N} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞N) = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ 0) = 0 (Hᵐ⌞N = 0 as Hᵐ(N) = 0; Measure.prod_zero, Measure.map_zero), and H^{m+1}({π ∈ N}) = (H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ N})({π ∈ N}) = 0. (D2) (product sets) If A satisfies the hypotheses of (MP), then ν_A := Hᵐ⌞A is finite on compact sets (ν_A(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ A), Measure.restrict_apply), hence σ-finite (instance SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), and H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)} = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν_A). Proof: {π ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)} = O ∩ {π ∈ A} and O is Borel, so H^{m+1}⌞(O ∩ {π ∈ A}) = (H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ A})⌞O (Measure.restrict_restrict) = (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν_A))⌞O (MP) = Φ′_*((L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞Φ′⁻¹(O)) (Measure.restrict_map, Φ′ measurable) and Φ′⁻¹(O) = (0,1) × E by (F1), so (L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞((0,1) × E) = (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ (ν_A⌞E) = (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν_A (Measure.prod_restrict, Measure.restrict_univ).

1. (Local finiteness.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. θ is integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn, K ⊆ univ) and θ ≥ 1 on M; M ∩ K is null-measurable, so 1 ≤ |θ| holds Hᵐ⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀) and Hᵐ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dHᵐ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} |θ| dHᵐ < ∞ (lintegral_mono_ae; finiteness of the integral of an integrable function). Hence ν := Hᵐ⌞M is finite on compacts and σ-finite, and M satisfies the hypotheses of (MP) (null-measurable and countably m-rectifiable by the triple). For every Hᵐ-null-measurable A ⊆ M the same holds (CountablyRectifiable.mono; Hᵐ(A ∩ K) ≤ Hᵐ(M ∩ K)), so (D2) applies to A. In particular H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*ρ with ρ := (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν.
2. (The contraction ℒ and the orientation ξ′.) ι : E → E′ is linear by (F2), hence a continuous linear map (finite dimension; LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Let ℒ := compContinuousLinearMapCLM ι ∘L (evaluation at e₀) ∘L curryLeftLI : Λ^{m+1}(E′) →L Λ^m(E). By curryLeft_apply_apply, ℒ(α)(v) = α.curryLeft(e₀)(ι ∘ v) = α(Matrix.vecCons e₀ (ι ∘ v)) = α(Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ v)) = α(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_m) (this holds by rfl). Define ξ′(y) := ξ(π(y)) ∘L ℒ ∈ NVector E′ (m+1), so ξ′(y)(α) = ξ(π(y))(ℒα).
3. (Characterization.) Let s, x, α, β with β(v) = α(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_m) for all v. Then ℒα = β (ext, Step 2) and π(Φ(s, x)) = x (F1), so ξ′(Φ(s, x))(α) = ξ(x)(ℒα) = ξ(x)(β). This is the second conjunct. It remains to verify the seven fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ (m+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ′.
4. (subset) M̃ ⊆ univ.
5. (nullMeasurableSet) M is Hᵐ-null-measurable, so there is a Borel M_B with M =ᵐ M_B, i.e. N := M Δ M_B has Hᵐ(N) = 0. The set where y ∈ {π ∈ M} and y ∈ {π ∈ M_B} disagree is {π ∈ N}, which is H^{m+1}-null by (D1); so {π ∈ M} =ᵐ {π ∈ M_B}, and {π ∈ M_B} is Borel (π continuous). Hence {π ∈ M} is H^{m+1}-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.congr), and so is M̃ = O ∩ {π ∈ M} (O open).
6. (countablyRectifiable) By the triple, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : Eucl m → E K_j-Lipschitz. Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))); π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))); y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0; Φ′ : ℝ × E → E′, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = Φ(1, 0); ι(v) := Φ(0, v); M̃ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)}; θ̃ := θ ∘ π (Lean: fun y => θ (π y)); O := {y ∈ E′ : y₀ ∈ (0,1)} (open), so M̃ = O ∩ {π ∈ M}. (MP) denotes the hypothesis: for every A ⊆ E that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A).
Coordinate facts (all by Fin.cons/Fin.tail computations, ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_self_tail): (F1) π(Φ(s,u)) = u, (Φ(s,u))₀ = s and Φ(y₀, π(y)) = y; (F2) Φ is linear; (F3) ⟨Φ(a,u), Φ(b,w)⟩ = ab + ⟨u,w⟩; (F4) Φ′ is a homeomorphism ℝ × E → E′ with continuous inverse y ↦ (y₀, π(y)) (Continuous.finCons, continuous_pi), hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding); in particular Φ′ and π are Borel measurable.
Derived fact from (MP) used below. (D2) (product sets) If A satisfies the hypotheses of (MP), then ν_A := Hᵐ⌞A is finite on compact sets (ν_A(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ A), Measure.restrict_apply), hence σ-finite (instance SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), and H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)} = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν_A). Proof: {π ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)} = O ∩ {π ∈ A} and O is Borel, so H^{m+1}⌞(O ∩ {π ∈ A}) = (H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ A})⌞O (Measure.restrict_restrict) = (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν_A))⌞O (MP) = Φ′_*((L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞Φ′⁻¹(O)) (Measure.restrict_map, Φ′ measurable) and Φ′⁻¹(O) = (0,1) × E by (F1), so (L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞((0,1) × E) = (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ (ν_A⌞E) = (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν_A (Measure.prod_restrict, Measure.restrict_univ).

1. (Local finiteness.) For compact K: θ is integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn) and θ ≥ 1 on M; M ∩ K is null-measurable, so 1 ≤ |θ| Hᵐ⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀) and Hᵐ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} |θ| dHᵐ < ∞. Hence M satisfies the hypotheses of (MP) (null-measurable and countably m-rectifiable by the triple), and ν := Hᵐ⌞M is finite on compacts, hence σ-finite.
2. (Measure identity.) By (D2) with A = M: H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*ρ, ρ := (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν.
3. (Transport.) Let F(y) := θ(π(y))·ξ′(y)(η(y)). By definition tauAction (m+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ′ η = ∫ F d(H^{m+1}⌞M̃) = ∫ F d(Φ′_*ρ) = ∫ F∘Φ′ dρ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, valid for every integrand since Φ′ is a measurable embedding (F4)).
4. (Integrability.) By hypothesis F is integrable for H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*ρ, so F∘Φ′ is ρ-integrable (MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff).
5. (Fubini.) By integral_prod, ∫ F∘Φ′ dρ = ∫_{(0,1)} (∫_M F(Φ(s, x)) dHᵐ(x)) ds.
6. (Pointwise identification.) Let s ∈ (0, 1) ⊆ [0, 1] and x ∈ ℝ^P. By (F1), π(Φ(s, x)) = x. Put α := η(Φ(s, x)) and β := φ(s)(x). Hence F(Φ(s, x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) for every x, and ∫_M F(Φ(s, x)) dHᵐ(x) = ∫_M θ ξ(φ(s)) dHᵐ = tauAction m M θ ξ (φ s) for every s ∈ (0, 1) (setIntegral_congr_fun on the Borel set (0, 1), integral_congr_ae).

MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integrable_map_iff move the integral and the integrability hypothesis to the product measure.

subproblems.title: τ(M, θ, ξ) of a rectifiable triple is a current (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V, M ⊆ ℝ^P (V arbitrary), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P) with IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ. Then τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ defines a current: there is X ∈ Dₙ(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n) with X(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration br_loc_tauAction_current, node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.localization-a1.tau_current-a1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn V n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration br_loc_tauAction_current (node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.localization-a1.tau_current-a1); the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. The two auxiliary facts that the accepted proof cites (the integrability statement of ltg_tau_integrable (b) and the unit bound fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound) are proved inline in Steps 1–2, so the argument below is self-contained. In the parent it is applied with V = ℝ^{P+1}, n = m + 1 and the product triple (M̃, θ∘π, ξ′); this is Step 4 of the parent proof.

Notation. H := Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α (continuous alternating map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm. For ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) (TestFormOn V n: C^∞, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V) put F_ω(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) and τ(ω) := tauAction n M θ ξ ω = ∫_M F_ω dH. Openness of V is never used.

1. (Unit bound.) By the field orients, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ; then for every n-covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j ‖τ_j‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the empty product is 1 when n = 0). Moreover H⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (M is H-null-measurable, ae_restrict_mem₀), and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (field pos). Let G be the set of x ∈ M at which the bound holds; H⌞M-a.e. x lies in G.
2. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) and K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of V. The map x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (the evaluation (w, α) ↦ w(α) is continuous, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable) and ω is continuous). ω is continuous with compact support, so ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x. θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn), and |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ C for H⌞M-a.e. x by Step 1; so F_ω is integrable on M ∩ K (Integrable.bdd_mul). F_ω vanishes on M ∖ K (ω = 0 off tsupport ω), and M is null-measurable, so F_ω is H-integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
3. (Linearity.) For ω, ω′ ∈ Dⁿ(V) and c ∈ ℝ, F_{ω+ω′} = F_ω + F_{ω′} and F_{cω} = c·F_ω pointwise (each ξ(x) is linear). By Step 2 and integral_add, τ(ω + ω′) = τ(ω) + τ(ω′); by integral_const_mul, τ(cω) = c·τ(ω). Hence L(ω) := τ(ω) is an ℝ-linear map Dⁿ(V) → ℝ.
4. (Uniform smallness.) Let (ω_j) converge to 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0): there is a compact K ⊆ V with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every iterated derivative converges uniformly on K. For order 0, ‖D⁰ω_j(x)‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). Hence for every δ > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K.
5. (Majorant.) θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn), and K is closed, hence Borel; so 1_K·θ is H⌞M-integrable and ∫_M 1_K θ dH = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH =: C (integrable_indicator_iff, integral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict).
6. (Estimate.) Let ε > 0, δ := ε/(|C| + 1) > 0, and j ≥ j₀ (Step 4 for this δ). For x ∈ G: if x ∈ K, then |F_{ω_j}(x)| = θ(x)|ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δθ(x) = δ1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K, then ω_j(x) = 0 (tsupport ω_j ⊆ K) and F_{ω_j}(x) = 0 = δ1_K(x)θ(x). So |F_{ω_j}| ≤ δ1_Kθ H⌞M-a.e., and |L(ω_j)| ≤ ∫_M δ1_Kθ dH = δC ≤ δ|C| < ε (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
7. (Continuity.) Step 6 shows L(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(V); this is the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn V n.
8. (Conclusion.) X := ⟨L, Step 7⟩ ∈ Dₙ(V) and X(ω) = L(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). ∎
proof_key_steps: Orientation gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x; θ > 0 on M.
For a test form ω, x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is integrable on M (bounded measurable factor times θ on M ∩ tsupport ω, zero elsewhere), so ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(V), supports lie in one compact K and sup_K‖ω_j‖ → 0, so |τ(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K‖ω_j‖·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0.
The linear sequentially continuous functional is the required current.

subproblems.title: Integrability of θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ on M for a rectifiable triple (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) with IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ; H := Hᵏ = μHE[k]. (a) For every compact K ⊆ U and every k-covector b, x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K. (b) For every continuous k-covector field ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ(ℝ^P) with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U, x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration ltg_tau_integrable, node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.local_to_global_im-a1.tau_integrable-a1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k), IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → (∀ (K : Set (Eucl P)) (b : Covector (Eucl P) k), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn (fun x => θ x * ξ x b) (M ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P))) ∧ ∀ ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) k, Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → tsupport ω ⊆ U → IntegrableOn (fun x => θ x * ξ x (ω x)) M (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration ltg_tau_integrable (node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.local_to_global_im-a1.tau_integrable-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. In the parent, part (b) is applied to the product triple and the test form η to obtain the integrability hypothesis of the sibling slice_formula.

Notation. H := μHE[k]. For a k-covector α (a continuous alternating k-linear map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm, so |α(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |v_j|. The fields of IsRectifiableTriple used are nullMeasurableSet, integrableOn, aestronglyMeasurable and orients.

1. (Unit bound.) For H⌞M-a.e. x and every k-covector α: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖. By orients, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. Since simpleNVector τ (α) = α(τ₁,…,τ_k), we get |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |τ_j| = ‖α‖, because |τ_j| = 1. For k = 0 the empty product is 1.
2. (Measurability.) Let ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ be continuous. The evaluation map Λ_k × Λᵏ → ℝ, (w, α) ↦ w(α), is continuous. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M (aestronglyMeasurable), and ω is continuous. Hence x ↦ (ξ(x), ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M, and so is its composition x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) with the evaluation map. The same holds for H⌞S whenever S ⊆ M, since H⌞S ≤ H⌞M. Taking ω constant equal to b gives the same for x ↦ ξ(x)(b).
3. (Part (a).) Let K ⊆ U be compact and b a k-covector. By integrableOn, θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K. Since M ∩ K ⊆ M, step 1 gives |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x. By step 2, x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K). The product of an integrable function with an a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded function is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul). So x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
4. (Part (b) on the support.) Let ω be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. Put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U. Being continuous with compact support, ω is bounded: |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x. θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (integrableOn). x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K) (step 2), and |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x (step 1). As in step 3, h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
5. (Part (b), conclusion.) If x ∈ M ∖ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and h(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. M is H-null-measurable (nullMeasurableSet) and M ∩ K ⊆ M. A function integrable on M ∩ K that vanishes on M ∖ (M ∩ K) is integrable on the null-measurable set M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). Hence h is H-integrable on M. ∎
proof_key_steps: Orientation (ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_k, τ orthonormal) gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for H⌞M-a.e. x and every covector α.
x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable: continuous evaluation composed with (ξ, ω).
An integrable function (θ on M ∩ K) times an a.e.-bounded measurable factor is integrable; this gives (a), and (b) on M ∩ tsupport ω.
The integrand of (b) vanishes on M ∖ tsupport ω, so it is integrable on the null-measurable set M.

subproblems.title: Change of variables under the blow-up map η_{x,r} (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0, S ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set and g : ℝ^P → ℝ an arbitrary function, and η := blowUpMap x r, η(z) = r⁻¹(z − x). Then ∫_{η(S)} g dH = (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z) (Bochner set integrals; no measurability or integrability assumption). (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral, node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.tangent_locality-a1.blowup_change_of_variables-a1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ) (S : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in S, g (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral (node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.tangent_locality-a1.blowup_change_of_variables-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. In this decomposition it is used by the sibling product_tangent to undo the blow-ups in ℝ^{P+1} (n = m + 1) and in ℝ^P (n = m).

Notation: H := μHE[n] and η := blowUpMap x r, η(z) = r⁻¹ • (z − x), with r > 0.

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. It is continuous, and w ↦ x + r • w is a continuous two-sided inverse: r⁻¹ • ((x + r•w) − x) = w and x + r • (r⁻¹ • (z − x)) = z, using r ≠ 0. Hence η is a bijection and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
2. Scaling of preimages. For every set F ⊆ ℝ^P, η⁻¹(F) = τ_x(r • F), where τ_x(w) = x + w (IsometryEquiv.addLeft x) and r • F = {r•w : w ∈ F}. Indeed z ∈ η⁻¹(F) iff w := r⁻¹ • (z − x) ∈ F, and then z = x + r • w. Translation is an isometry, so H(τ_x(E)) = H(E) for every set E (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Also H(r • F) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ · H(F) = rⁿ · H(F) for every set F (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, r ≠ 0). Therefore H(η⁻¹(F)) = rⁿ · H(F) for every F ⊆ ℝ^P.
3. Push-forward identity: map η (H⌞S) = rⁿ · H⌞η(S). Let E be measurable. Then η⁻¹(E) is measurable, and (map η (H⌞S))(E) = (H⌞S)(η⁻¹(E)) = H(η⁻¹(E) ∩ S) by Measure.map_apply and Measure.restrict_apply. Since η is a bijection, η⁻¹(E) ∩ S = η⁻¹(E ∩ η(S)). By step 2 this is rⁿ · H(E ∩ η(S)) = rⁿ · (H⌞η(S))(E). Measures agreeing on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext).
4. Change of variables along a measurable embedding needs no integrability (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). It gives ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫ (g ∘ η) d(H⌞S) = ∫ g d(map η (H⌞S)).
5. By step 3 and integral_smul_measure (∫ g d(c·μ) = c.toReal · ∫ g dμ for every g and c ∈ [0,∞]): ∫ g d(map η (H⌞S)) = rⁿ · ∫ g d(H⌞η(S)) = rⁿ · ∫_{η(S)} g dH. Here the scalar (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) has toReal equal to rⁿ.
6. Steps 4 and 5 give rⁿ · ∫_{η(S)} g dH = ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z). Since rⁿ > 0, multiplying by (rⁿ)⁻¹ yields ∫_{η(S)} g dH = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z). ∎
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is a homeomorphism with inverse w ↦ x + r•w, hence a bijective measurable embedding.
For every set F, η⁻¹(F) = x + r•F, so H(η⁻¹F) = rⁿH(F) by isometry invariance and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
map η (H⌞S) = rⁿ • H⌞η(S), checked on measurable E via η⁻¹(E) ∩ S = η⁻¹(E ∩ η(S)).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give rⁿ∫_{η(S)} g dH = ∫_S g∘η dH; divide by rⁿ > 0.
